title: A Guide to the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK Guide)
author: Project Management Institute
thesisParagraph: Project management is the disciplined adaptation of people, practices, governance, and tools to deliver value in changing systems. The Seventh Edition replaces a single process-first reading path with principles, performance domains, tailoring, and selectable practice assets.

signatureMoves: defines terms before giving application guidance
uses numbered principle and domain structures as the main teaching spine
repeats value, outcomes, tailoring, context, and systems language
contrasts predictive, adaptive, and hybrid approaches without making one universal
frames tools and artifacts by purpose rather than by mandatory use
avoidMoves: does not use memoir or dramatic narrative scenes
does not prescribe one lifecycle for every project
does not equate document production with project success
does not treat project work as isolated from governance, products, operations, or stakeholders

teachingArc: The expanded opening teaches value delivery as a system, including governance, project functions, environment, and product considerations. The middle turns the 12 PMBOK principles into individual behavioral units, then maps the 8 performance domains as ongoing areas of project health. The close explains tailoring and the three practice-asset categories so readers can select models, methods, and artifacts for context rather than copy a checklist.
